M_SWB.evidence_source: [/page/9/Text/5] The mean level of father's life satisfaction in the year preceding the birth of a child (time 0) is not significantly different between the two groups, with fathers who eventually took parental leave having a mean life satisfaction of 3.69 and fathers who did not take parental leave having a mean life satisfaction of 3.71 (t = −0.46, df = 156, p > .05). There was a significant difference in life satisfaction between these two groups at T1, where the mean life satisfaction of fathers who used parental leave increased to 3.85 while that of fathers who did not use parental leave decreased to 3.63 (t = −2.65, df = 184, p < .01). Further, this difference in life satisfaction persisted in T2 with fathers who took parental leave having a mean life satisfaction score of 3.79, compared to 3.60 among fathers who did not take parental leave (t = −2.18, df = 170, p < .05).
